_comment: What the wordplay capability adds to the screens for any pack that lists "wordplay" in its capabilities. A pack may patch any of these by key (same rules as its own vocabulary).

anagram-pair.label: Anagram pairs
anagram-pair.blurb: Two names made from exactly the same letters.

one-letter-off.label: One letter apart
one-letter-off.blurb: Two names that differ by a single letter.

head-tail.label: Letter dropped
head-tail.blurb: A name that becomes another word when its first or last letter is dropped.

homophone.label: Sound-alikes
homophone.blurb: A name and an everyday word that sound exactly alike.

anagram-of-word.label: Anagram of a word
anagram-of-word.blurb: A name whose letters rearrange into an everyday word.

hidden-word.label: Hidden word
hidden-word.blurb: A name with another word hiding inside it.

reversal.label: Backwards
reversal.blurb: A name that spells another name when read backwards.

digit-lookalike.label: Digit look-alike
digit-lookalike.blurb: A name where letters stand in for digits.

features.blurb: Two blocks that stay put: Facts (narrow by how well connected and what connects; All shelves and All kinds zoom back out) and Results (shuffled by default, or ordered by a lens, with Starred only) and Wordplay (pairs of names by trick). The results below follow the one you touched last.

recipes.title: I want to find names and words that echo each other
recipes.goal: Find pairs of names and words that echo each other by sound or by letters: anagrams, hidden words, near-spellings.
steps: In the Wordplay block on {home}, pick a trick: Sound-alikes, One letter apart, Letter dropped, Anagram pairs, Anagram of a word, Hidden word, Backwards or Digit look-alike. All wordplay shows every kind together.
Each tile is one pair, such as a name and the everyday word it sounds like. Open one to see the facts about it.
On the set page press {star} this pair to save it to {starred}, or Dull if the pair is only chance.
To build on it, press {focus} on one of its facts, then {collect} the facts that fit the trick (see the recipe on writing the link line).
recipes.then: Pairs come from a detector that guesses, so expect some chance matches; Dull and Wrong sense teach nothing to the detector but keep them out of your way.
